newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania facing food crisis very soon - minister.
newsitem.headline: Albania facing food crisis very soon - minister.

text.p: Albania faces a serious food crisis because of looting of government reserves and the collapse of the trading system during the current unrest, Finance Minister Arben Malaj said on Tuesday.
The minister, appointed only last week, told a news conference he had asked a visiting European Union delegation for urgent financial assistance to help the country out of its troubles.
Speaking after meeting members of the delegation, headed by a senior Dutch diplomat, the minister declined to say how much he had requested but said delegation members had responded with "shock".
The Swiss-based International Committee of the Red Cross put a financial figure on Albania's crisis on Tuesday with an appeal to donors for $10.3 million for urgentlly needed food and medicine.
Malaj said he had no exact figures on the food situation, but added: "It is clear that very soon we will be facing a crisis. The government stocks are gone and the trading system is not functioning."
Asked whether he had the impression the West would respond to Tirana's request for money, Malaj said that since the delegation put several conditions on aid, he believed it would be forthcoming.
- Clarifying the situation surrounding collapsed pyramid savings schemes that bankrupted thousands.
- The re-establishment of relations with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which would have to approve any EU aid to the country.

The minister said an estimated $1 billion had been lost in the fraudulent schemes, whose collapse earlier this year sparked an armed rebellion in the south that spread unrest right across the country.
However he said a final figure would not be known until a complete audit of the companies' books now under way was completed.

Malaj defended the government's recent decision to pay huge wages -- up to $100 a day or 30 times average earnings -- to special police units to go out and disarm gunmen who threatened the country with total anarchy.
The minister said that if the units succeeded in preventing 15,000 tonnes of grain out of 80,000 tonnes from being looted, they would have paid their way.
Malaj said there was an urgent need to restore financial institutions across Albania and reopen and secure the main ports of Durres and Vlore, where chaos now reigns.
"If we fail to take such steps then I'm very pessimistic about our capacity to normalise the situation and enable foreign institutions to help us," he said.
